messages:

Subject: Quick question on pilot extension / SKU bundling

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the pilot setup — the team has been happy with the latency and integration speed. A couple procurement/legal items came up as we plan next steps: 1) we want to extend the current time-boxed pilot by an additional 4 weeks; 2) we'd prefer to move to a small SKU bundle during the extension (flat monthly bucket vs per-token), and 3) our CFO asked whether there is an "early termination" credit if we convert early to a committed package or stop the pilot before the full extension.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will:
- allow a 4-week extension on the same trial terms,
- provide a quoted SKU bundle price for the extension period, and
- what the policy is on early-conversion/termination credits?

We can share estimated usage numbers if that helps.

Best,

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes to a 4-week extension; yes we can propose a SKU-bundle option for that window; and yes, we have a limited early-conversion credit structure (depends on how you convert). Below I outline options and next steps.

1) Extension: We can extend the existing pilot for 4 weeks on the same SOW and terms. We typically require an amendment to the SOW (1–2 pager) signed by both parties; I attached a one-page amendment draft (redwood_pilot_terms_draft.docx).

2) SKU bundling for extension: Two common patterns we offer for short extensions:
  - Timebox-flat: flat monthly bucket (e.g., 200k tokens/month) priced as a short-term SKU bundle. Good if your usage is predictable.
  - Usage-offset: we keep per-token billing but offer a blended discount band for the extension. Better if you expect bursty traffic.

I've asked Ben to attach a pricing matrix for both options with sample numbers based on the usage snapshot you shared.

3) Early-conversion / termination credit: We offer an early-conversion credit when a customer converts from pilot to a committed Reserved bundle within the extension period. Typical structure for pilots this size: 50% of unused paid extension SKU value can be applied as a one-time credit against the first month of committed capacity, or we can pro-rate into the committed SKU price depending on the contract. If you terminate without converting, there is no refund for already-consumed extension fees (standard).

Next steps: Ben will follow up with pricing scenarios. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the matrix and pick an approach.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0129

Hi all — attaching a quick pricing_matrix.xlsx (see tabs: Timebox-flat, Usage-offset, Credit-scenarios). Summary of the recommended scenarios based on ByteWorks' week-3 snapshot:
  - Scenario A (Timebox-flat): 250k token bucket / 4 weeks at $5,200 flat. Includes 10% overage at $0.00004/token.
  - Scenario B (Usage-offset): blended per-token rate $0.000055 with a 12% discount on observed consumption. Estimated spend for 4 weeks: ~$4,700 (variable).
  - Early-conversion credit: if you convert to a 6-month reserved package by the end of the extension, we will apply 50% of any unused portion of the Timebox-flat fee as a one-time credit to month 1 of the committed billing. Credit can also be spread over month 1–2 if you prefer.

Notes / caveats: credits are only available for conversions to reserved/committed SKUs (not to continued on-demand). If legal needs different language we can add specific definitions of "conversion" in the amendment.

If you want the SKU priced as a per-seat equivalent rather than tokens, we can attempt that but it'll be an approximation. Happy to jump on a call — I'm available 10–12 PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
